newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Notionnel vols ease, Pibor stays high.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Notionnel vols ease, Pibor stays high.

text.p: Implied volatility of notionnel options eased on Tuesday after shooting higher on the surprise win by left-wing parties in French elections but Pibor volatility stayed high, brokers said.
Brokers said the market would likely remain on tenterhooks and volatility well supported until the second round of the election next Sunday.

"Yesterday, obviously volatility was pretty nicely bid but the only thing we saw was people selling options all day...and selling volatility down," Jonathan Morris, options broker at Finacor in Paris, said.
"So today I'm seeing volatility ease a little bit once again," he said.
Brokers quoted implied volatility of July notionnel options at around 6.30 percent compared with a high of around 6.75 percent on Monday and 5.95 percent on Friday.
September volatility was quoted round 5.45 percent, versus highs of around 5.80 percent on Monday and 5.30 percent on Friday.
June notionnel options expire on Thursday.
At the short end, at-the-money June Pibor straddles were quoted with a volatility of around 58 percent, up from around 40 percent on Friday and attracting buyers.

French markets were caught on the hop by Sunday's election result. Left wing parties racked up 44 percent of the votes, including the Greens, leaving the ruling centre-right coalition and moderate rightists with only 36.5 and questions over France's future EMU strategy.
By 1315 GMT, June notionnel futures were quoted unchanged at 128.30, but down 70 basis points from Friday.
June Pibor futures, had regained some poise to trade up 0.06 at 96.27 but were still 20 basis points off Friday's close.
"I've seen pretty much two-way traffic," Morris said."People are looking at this the same way they're looking at the election -- it's going to go either way," he said.
He said one trade that reflected election strategy was the buying of July calls and selling of June calls, with investors expecting the market to drop off before it rebounded once again.
Luke White, options broker at Fimat Banque in London, added, "A lot of people have been looking at strategies but not in huge sizes," he said.
He noted one investor buying the 126.00 July notionnel and selling the 124.00 in a put spread for a total of 2,000 lots.
Elsewhere investors were pulling out of June strikes and into July to avoid the uncertainty. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
